claims.statement: Attackers asked Meta's AI support assistant to link an attacker-controlled email address to a target Instagram account, then used a password reset to take the account over.
The assistant did not perform robust identity verification; a VPN set to a location near the account owner was reported to be enough.
Meta said the issue was resolved and that it was securing impacted accounts; Reuters reported Meta shares fell more than 5% afterward.
Android Authority reported about 34,000 affected accounts; other coverage gives no authoritative count.
404 Media, as relayed by MacRumors, said hackers had known about the exploit since March 2026.

unresolvedQuestions: Primary source needed: Meta's statement is known only through news quotes (Andy Stone on X, June 1, 2026); the original 404 Media report was not checked directly.
Disputed: affected-account count (about 34,000 per Android Authority; a figure of more than 20,000 is cited by Straiker; most outlets give no count).
Disputed: whether two-factor authentication stopped takeovers. Engadget says 2FA accounts got reset requests but were not taken over; other reports say 2FA was bypassed.
Unknown: root cause beyond reported weak verification, and whether Meta attributes it to the model or the surrounding verification system.
